correctness.rationale: Every connected simple leafless bicyclic graph has exactly one degree-four branch or two degree-three branches. Suppressing degree-two paths gives respectively a figure-eight, a theta, or a barbell. Equality of C2 colours at marked roots forces equality of multisets of distances to the next marked root in the universal covering tree. This determines all parameters except a symmetric barbell versus a theta with matching two repeated path lengths. An explicit balanced equitable vertex partition, with matching class sizes, proves all such pairs C2-equivalent, and bridges distinguish their isomorphism types. The count for order n follows by a direct integer-interval count. Two packaged programs confirm the exhaustive small-order and structured-parametric finite cases; no infinite statement is inferred solely from computation.

value.rationale: This completes the natural first nontrivial two-cycle core class: an explicit all-order logical-equivalence classification with exactly counted doubletons, showing a structural failure to distinguish a bridgeless theta from a bridge-containing barbell. The six-vertex sharp onset and exact family of ambiguities are useful benchmarks for finite model theory and equitable graph partitions. Unlike a random small census, the result explains a pervasive infinite mechanism and fully describes its scope.
